author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend completed a career Grand Slam as a team Friday, rallying to win the U.S. Open women's doubles final 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 over American wild cards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery in New York.

The top-seeded pair recovered decisively after dropping the first set. Early in the second, they won 23 of 27 points to force a deciding set, then consolidated an early break as Townsend held for a 4-2 lead. The turnaround erased a difficult opening frame in which Siniakova double-faulted three times while serving to force a tiebreak.

Siniakova and Townsend had already won Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and the French Open earlier this year. Adding the U.S. Open made them champions at all four majors together. The victory was Siniakova's 12th Grand Slam doubles title and made her the first player to complete a team career Grand Slam with two different partners; she previously accomplished the feat with Barbora Krejcikova. For Townsend, the title completed a partnership arc that included a runner-up finish in New York last year.
dek: The top seeds rallied past Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery in three sets to capture the U.S. Open women's doubles title.
headline: Siniakova and Townsend complete team career Grand Slam
